name: Canyon Moon Palace — interior and court sections
prompt:
Create ONE clean detailed GAME ASSET REFERENCE SHEET, NOT Blender or a3Dmodel. Plain light ivory studio background, soft even light, full uncropped separate objects, readable thickness, precise non-melting forms. FULL IDs and names outside silhouettes, dimensions marked PROPOSED. Each cell independent illustration scale. No environment scenery, humans, extra unlabeled objects, watermark or whole-palace redesign. Use ONLY the single supplied source image for visible style/material/form authority; infer missing backs and assembly interfaces conservatively. Source illustration motifs are inspiration, not recovered measured geometry. Visible source facts: Apricot sandstone palace attached to a vertical canyon shelf, turquoise onion domes, tall star banners, huge circular gilded moon screen/entry and water spilling between lower arches/rock piers. Iso climbs along the cliff; mini-plan is elongated with rounded room/tower ends. Hidden layout inference: A lower ledge arrival climbs a switchback garden stair to the moon-screen court, then to one sheltered upper dome terrace. Separate dry cliff-edge overlooks from lush irrigated court pockets; channels feed controlled falls and stay away from walking edges. Back depth/return route are inferred. Preserve this local design. Exactly4 large cells, large three-quarter view for each module plus small front, top and side/contact/section diagram consistent with same geometry. Real open doors/arches/windows must show empty space; no opaque filling where an opening is requested. Continuous unobstructed planar joining ends, separate shells from optional decor, no fused unrelated objects. Hollow roof/room sections show the interior underside and wall thickness. Keep source silhouette, not generic boxes. Title "B10-INNER-001 — Canyon Moon Palace — interior and court sections". Footer "Proposed construction / source-compatible references / mesh joins and views unverified".

Purpose/gap: Missing interior construction and local court transitions beyond exterior sections
